facts.value: The rules were last updated July 30, 2026.
facts.quote: Last Updated: July 30, 2026

facts.value: Film qualifying year for the 84th: January 1 to December 31, 2026.
facts.quote: For the 84th Annual Golden Globes, the qualifying year shall be January 1 through December 31, 2026.

facts.value: Eligible films: scripted features of 70 minutes or longer, released and made available to all voters in the qualifying year.
facts.quote: Feature-length, scripted motion pictures (70 minutes or longer) that have been both released and made available for viewing to all Golden Globes voters pursuant to these rules during the qualifying year (January 1 through December 31).

facts.value: Released means a seven-day consecutive commercial run (theatrical or pay-per-view, not subscription) in one of seven US metro areas, starting before 11:59 p.m. on December 31.
facts.quote: made available for public exhibition in commercial motion picture theaters or on a recognized platform pay-per-view cable channel or pay-per-view digital delivery service (not subscription cable or digital delivery) in any of the greater Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City or San Francisco metropolitan areas for a minimum seven-day consecutive period beginning prior to 11:59 p.m. local time on December 31 of the qualifying year.

facts.value: A festival screening is not a release unless it meets the run criteria.
facts.quote: A motion picture exhibited at a film festival would not qualify as “released” unless it meets the criteria set forth above.

facts.value: A film must be entered for Best Motion Picture for its individuals (including performers) to be eligible.
facts.quote: A motion picture must be eligible and submitted for consideration in the Best Motion Picture category in order to be eligible for consideration in any of the individual award categories set forth below

facts.value: Non-English-language and low-budget independent films may enter performers without entering Best Motion Picture.
facts.quote: However, Non-English Language and low-budget independent motion pictures may be submitted for individual Best Performance categories without being submitted in the Best Motion Picture category, provided they meet all other eligibility requirements.

facts.value: Low-budget independent means fully independently financed and a gross production budget under $10 million USD.
facts.quote: (a) is fully financed by independent producers, private investors, or small production companies, and (b) has a gross production budget of less than $10 million USD.

facts.value: Voice-only performances are not eligible in any film performance category.
facts.quote: Voice-only performances and other roles in which the actor’s face is not visible are not eligible in any performance category.

facts.value: Lead: central characters in a substantial portion who drive the narrative.
facts.quote: Lead cast members in a motion picture must be the central characters who appear in a substantial portion of the motion picture and who drive the narrative of the motion picture.

facts.value: Supporting: non-central characters who support the leads or narrative.
facts.quote: Supporting cast members in a motion picture are the non-central characters who support the lead characters and/or the narrative of the motion picture.

facts.value: Performers in English or non-English films may qualify.
facts.quote: Performers appearing in either English language or non-English language motion pictures may qualify for performance awards.

facts.value: A non-English film must be classified Drama or Musical/Comedy for its performers to be eligible.
facts.quote: In order for individual performers from a non-English language motion picture to be eligible for Best Performance categories, the applicable non-English language motion picture must be classified as either a Drama or Musical/Comedy.

facts.value: Non-English films from outside the US need no US release for the Non-English Language award.
facts.quote: Non-English-language motion pictures that originate outside the United States do not need to be released in the United States to qualify for the Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language award.

facts.value: For the Non-English Language award, a first release in the country of origin for at least seven consecutive days in the qualifying year.
facts.quote: a motion picture must be first released in its country of origin during the qualifying calendar year for a minimum seven-day consecutive period.

facts.value: TV: first aired or made available in the US in the qualifying year in prime time.
facts.quote: Only programs first aired (or made available for viewing on demand) in the United States during the qualifying year (January 1 through December 31) in prime time (8:00 p.m. – 11:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday; 7:00 p.m. – 11:00 p.m. Sunday) are eligible for television awards.

facts.value: Cable and subscription platforms are exempt from the prime-time rule.
facts.quote: Programs released on cable or subscription-based platforms are exempt from the prime time requirement, provided they are first made available in the United States during the qualifying year.

facts.value: Foreign TV programs are ineligible unless a US-foreign co-production (financial and creative) that precedes completion.
facts.quote: Foreign programs (programs produced principally outside the United States) are not eligible for television awards unless they are the result of a co-production (both financially and creatively) between a United States partner and a foreign partner, which precedes the completion of production of the program.

facts.value: TV eligibility does not depend on language.
facts.quote: The eligibility of television programs does not depend on the language(s) used in the program.

facts.value: Animated TV programs may enter the series categories.
facts.quote: Animated television programs may be entered in the appropriate category (Best Series – Drama, Best Series – Musical or Comedy, etc.) if they meet the other qualifying criteria for that category.

facts.value: A TV program first shown at a festival is not disqualified.
facts.quote: A television program first exhibited at a festival would not be disqualified for television awards if it otherwise meets the television eligibility criteria set forth herein.

facts.value: A motion picture enters film or TV categories, not both, by original release format.
facts.quote: Motion pictures should be entered in either the motion picture or the television award categories (but not both) based on their original release format.

facts.value: A TV program must be entered in a Best Television category for its performers to be eligible (except stand-up).
facts.quote: a television program must be eligible and submitted for consideration in one of the Best Television award categories to be eligible for consideration in any of the individual Best Performance categories set forth below.

facts.value: Anthology leads must be in segments of at least 50% of running time; others may go supporting.
facts.quote: contributed to segments that comprise at least 50% of the running time in the anthology series. All other actors are eligible for the Best Performance in a Supporting Role awards if they meet the other requirements of these rules.

facts.value: The submitting studio or publicist initially selects the categories, including lead vs supporting.
facts.quote: The studio or publicist submitting a motion picture or television program initially selects the award categories for which it is entered (e.g., male actor vs. female actor, drama vs. musical/comedy or lead vs. supporting).

facts.value: The Eligibility and review committees may change an entry by a two-thirds vote.
facts.quote: These committees, voting by written ballot, may change any award entry by a vote of two-thirds or more of the committees’ members voting.

facts.value: Suspected misclassification: director/showrunner asked for a justification letter.
facts.quote: the Eligibility Committee will ask the director(s)/showrunner(s) of the motion picture or television program to submit a letter justifying the initial classification for review.

facts.value: All programming is submitted through Yangaroo and uploaded to the Indee platform.
facts.quote: all programming must be submitted through the Yangaroo submissions portal and uploaded to the Golden Globes Indee Viewing Platform.

facts.value: Individual performance entries need high-resolution photographs owned or controlled by the submitting party.
facts.quote: Entries for individual performance awards must be accompanied by submission of high-resolution photographs (e.g., head shot or key artwork) owned and/or controlled by the party submitting such individual.

facts.value: $250 per individual entry; $500 per film, TV program and other title entries.
facts.quote: Yangaroo submission fees for Golden Globes consideration are $250 for each individual entry submitted and $500 for each motion picture, television program, Stand-Up Comedy on Television, Cinematic and Box Office Achievement production, and Best Podcast submitted.

facts.value: An individual entered for several productions pays a fee for each entry.
facts.quote: Entries for individuals submitted for consideration for their work on multiple productions will be charged a fee for each entry.

facts.value: Indee upload administration fee: $5,000 per title.
facts.quote: Uploads to the Golden Globes Indee Viewing Platform are subject to an administration fee of $5,000 per title.

facts.value: Productions under $2 million may ask about fee alternatives.
facts.quote: Motion pictures, television programs, and Cinematic and Box Office Achievement films with production budgets of less than $2 million USD may contact AwardsOffice@GoldenGlobes.com to inquire about fee alternatives.

facts.value: Only individuals designated by Golden Globes, LLC vote.
facts.quote: Only individuals officially designated by the Company as Golden Globes voters (“Golden Globes voters”) vote for the Golden Globes.

facts.value: Voting in two phases, monitored by an accounting firm: nominations and final vote.
facts.quote: The voting is monitored by an accounting firm and is conducted in two phases – Nominations and Final Vote.

facts.value: Each voter votes for up to six nominees per film/TV category, in order of preference.
facts.quote: requesting that each of them vote for up to (i) six nominees for motion picture and television programs and Best Podcast entries and (ii) eight nominees for Best Cinematic and Box Office Achievement productions, in order of preference in each award category

facts.value: Nominees are the six selections with most votes.
facts.quote: The nominees in each category will be the six (or eight) selections in each category that receive the greatest number of votes on the nomination ballots.

facts.value: Rank points are used only to break ties.
facts.quote: The accounting firm will use the points assigned in the nomination rankings only in the event of ties.

facts.value: Final ballot: one vote per category.
facts.quote: requesting that each of them votes for one nominee in each category and return the completed ballot directly to the accounting firm.

facts.value: A final tie goes to the tied nominee with more nomination-ballot votes.
facts.quote: In the case of a tie in any category, the winner will be the one of the tied nominees on the final ballot that had the most votes on the

facts.value: If still tied, two winners.
facts.quote: there is still a tie in any category, two winners will be announced for that category.

facts.value: Performances substantially generated by AI are not eligible.
facts.quote: Submissions in which a performance is substantially generated or created by artificial intelligence are not eligible.

facts.value: Each individual nominee may buy one nomination certificate for $1,500.
facts.quote: Every individual nominee and co-nominee named for an award is eligible to purchase one nomination certificate for a fee of $1,500.

facts.value: An Australian individual: born in Australia, a passport holder/citizen, or a permanent resident of 5+ years.
facts.quote: Australian – when used to describe an individual, an individual who was born in Australia, or is a current passport holder/citizen, or has been a permanent resident for at least 5 years.

facts.value: Eligibility route (i): significant Australian content under the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.
facts.quote: contain “significant Australian content” for the purposes of section 376-65(2)(a)(i) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

facts.value: Route (ii): at least 51% Australian financing.
facts.quote: have at least 51% financing from Australian investors

facts.value: Route (iii): official co-production or Australian creative control.
facts.quote: be an official co-production (as per a formal agreement with Australia and an international territory) or produced under the creative control of Australians if an international collaboration has occurred outside of a formal treaty

facts.value: Route (iv): otherwise satisfy AFI/AACTA at their discretion (the rule goes on to list factors such as setting, story, key creatives, shooting and financing).
facts.quote: otherwise satisfy the AFI and AACTA, in their sole and absolute discretion, that the Production is an eligible Production

facts.value: A production entered before is ineligible again.
facts.quote: A Television Program or Film, (or an episode or season of a Television Program) which has been previously entered into the Awards is ineligible for entry into the current or any future Awards.

facts.value: Entry by the Producer or a representative of the production company or distributor/broadcaster.
facts.quote: Your entry should be completed by the Producer or a representative of the Production Company or Distributor/Broadcaster.

facts.value: Every producer must agree to the entry.
facts.quote: AACTA will only consider an Entry Form as valid if the submission of it has been agreed to by all of the Producers of a Production.

facts.value: Dates are on the AACTA website, not in the rule book.
facts.quote: Please refer to the AACTA website for current dates as they relate to eligibility periods and voting periods.

facts.value: Fees are on the website and entry form.
facts.quote: The fees payable in relation to each Award Category will be stated on the AACTA Website and the Entry Form relevant to the Award Category and may change from year to year.

facts.value: A production may enter one award category.
facts.quote: Productions may only be entered into one Award Category

facts.value: TV entries need both the broadcaster executive and the senior production executive to confirm the category.
facts.quote: All TV category entrants will require confirmation of their entered categorisation from both; a senior executive at their associated broadcaster; and the most senior production executive listed on the entry.

facts.quote: In order for a production category to proceed with the standard number of nominations, at least 8 entries must be received.

facts.value: Fewer than 8 entries: nominations may be cut to 4.
facts.quote: If less than 8 entries are received, the final number of nominated productions may be reduced to 4.

facts.value: 4 or fewer entries: no award.
